      <title>One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa</link>
      <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. Vanuatu's Environment Minister Ralph Regenvanu has called for changes to the UN climate summit process, accusing a small group of countries of blocking progress and warning that COP31 risks reversing previous commitments.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/cd8e0060-e3d0-11f1-9616-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7VU8WE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/cd8e0060-e3d0-11f1-9616-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7VU8WE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5df44426-e3bc-11f1-be92-6d9f3ae22326</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 02:00:39 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/cd8e0060-e3d0-11f1-9616-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7VU8WE.jpg">© Yasin Akgul, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Asia / Pacific</category><title>Xi-Trump-Putin talks live: China, US and Russia leaders to hold landmark three-way meeting</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20261119-xi-trump-putin-talks-live-china-us-russia-leaders-hold-landmark-three-way-meeting</link><description>
The leaders of China, the US and Russia are set to hold a first-of-its-kind trilateral meeting on Thursday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of an APEC summit. The meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, which Beijing said would involve "safeguarding world peace", has raised fears of a carve-up of the globe into "spheres of influence". Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9734827a-e3c9-11f1-8ccd-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T030408Z-2074341856-RC2RQOAJQ487-RTRMADP-3-APEC-SUMMIT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9734827a-e3c9-11f1-8ccd-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T030408Z-2074341856-RC2RQOAJQ487-RTRMADP-3-APEC-SUMMIT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ff3b55a4-e38f-11f1-829a-0dfdbe55b740</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 01:47:04 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9734827a-e3c9-11f1-8ccd-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T030408Z-2074341856-RC2RQOAJQ487-RTRMADP-3-APEC-SUMMIT.jpg">© Sergei Bobylyov, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>24-month matured Comté crowned world’s best cheese</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261118-24-month-matured-comt%C3%A9-crowned-world-s-best-cheese</link><description>
With its nutty flavour and smooth, supple texture, it was aged for two years in a former military fortress in eastern France. Comté, an unpasteurised cow’s milk cheese from the Jura Mountains, has beaten more than five thousand challengers to the top prize at the prestigious annual 'World Cheese Awards'. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington has the story.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1cb81224-e396-11f1-bbfa-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261118-221442-221615-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1cb81224-e396-11f1-bbfa-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261118-221442-221615-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2270dff2-e396-11f1-87b3-8b1d88fc9324</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 22:32:24 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Business</category><title>Inside Limoges City Hall devastated by arson attack</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/business/20261118-inside-limoges-city-hall-devastated-by-arson-attack</link><description>
Work is underway to restore the city hall of Limoges, in central France, which was devastated by an arson attack during riots on October 17. More than €1.7 million has been raised through an online fundraising campaign in the wake of the disaster. Also on the show, the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI has finally been released, with gamers in Oceania among the first to get a taste of the latest instalment in the video game franchise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a034574a-e39e-11f1-bfdd-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-fa1f6e70.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a034574a-e39e-11f1-bfdd-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-fa1f6e70.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6abb7c10-e39e-11f1-b18a-73c01f9d8f47</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 22:23:48 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Yuka ROYER</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

]]> <![CDATA[ Astronomers witness a star eating its companion in 1st-of-its-kind observation ]]> Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports.

As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now.

"Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean. We need sensitive telescopes monitoring the sky for a long time in order to catch this effect."

In the new study, the researchers investigated a red giant star designated WNTR23bzdiq, which is located about 2.5 million light-years away in the Andromeda galaxy. The star is about seven times heftier and 350 times wider than our own sun.

In 2023, using NASA's now-defunct NEOWISE space telescope and the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, the scientists noticed that this star was brightening. By analyzing previous records, they found that the red giant had gradually started growing more luminous in 2018.

The researchers had previously suggested this brightening potentially occurred because the giant star engulfed a companion star. As this companion spiraled toward the giant's core, it would generate friction, heat and light, explaining the increasing luminosity.

Then, near the end of 2025, the astronomers saw a giant eruption of light from this giant star. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observed the star just 47 days after that eruption, allowing the team to characterize the event in detail. The researchers now propose that this explosion happened when a companion star about 70% the sun's mass rammed into the giant's heart.

"I was absolutely flabbergasted when we saw this," Karambelkar said.

In the new study, the scientists estimated that the eruption expelled an amount of material equal to about 0.1 to 0.2 times the mass of the sun. "Stars engulfing their companions have been theorized for many decades, and this event provides the first observations of this theoretical prediction," Karambelkar said.

Although these findings suggest that two stars — a binary system nicknamed "Bao" — merged into one, "it is not the only possibility," Karambelkar said. "The other possibility is that both stars survived, in a much shorter orbit. In order to conclusively determine what happened, we need to continue monitoring what the system does, once the heft of the eruption settles down."

Now that astronomers may have found the first such merger, "I can't wait to find more," Karambelkar said. "Upcoming telescopes like the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Vera Rubin Observatory will be very useful in discovering many more such events."

The scientists detailed their findings Nov. 18 in the journal Nature.

]]> <![CDATA[ Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why ]]> More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished.

Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past.

Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth.

Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years.

But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged.

One of the most striking examples is found in the Grand Canyon, where rocks separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, as if some force or phenomenon removed the layers that geologists would expect to see in between. This enormous gap in Earth's geological timeline is part of the phenomenon known as the Great Unconformity.

It's not just the Grand Canyon. Similar gaps have been identified across Europe, Australia, Africa and Asia. Depending on the location, the missing interval ranges from approximately 200 million years to more than a billion years.

"Imagine a book where a huge section in the middle has been ripped out," study lead author Santosh Dhungana said in a statement.

"The Great Unconformity is that gap in Earth's story, with the narrative jumping from the early chapters straight to a much later part of the story. Our research suggests these pages weren't lost by chance."

What erased the geological record?

In a new study published in the journal Nature, Dhungana and study co-author Nicolas Flament investigated whether activity far below Earth's surface was to blame.

Using computer models, they explored how the slow circulation of hot rock within Earth's mantle may have affected the continents over hundreds of millions of years.

The results suggest that three major ancient continental regions (Laurentia (modern North America), Baltica (northern Europe) and North China were gradually pushed up during the Neoproterozoic Era, approximately one billion to 540 million years ago.

This would have left vast areas of land exposed to weathering and erosion for long periods, allowing water, wind and other processes to wear away rock that had formed much earlier.

But removing the rock is only part of the puzzle. They also needed to explain why the gaps are still visible today.

Their models suggest that the same regions subsequently began to sink. As sea levels rose relative to the land, sediment accumulated over the older, eroded surfaces, creating the sharp divide between ancient and younger rocks that we can still see today.

Crucially, the researchers found that the timing of the simulated continental uplift and sinking was consistent with geological evidence from North America, northern Europe and North China. This suggests that movements deep within Earth's mantle may have played a major role in shaping the geological record we see today.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'A shotgun marriage': Why are NASA's SkyFall Mars helicopters riding on a nuclear rocket? ]]> The pace is picking up on building, testing, and plotting out the flight paths for a trio of NASA Ingenuity-class helicopters to investigate Mars after riding there on a nuclear-powered rocket.

NASA's Skyfall mission will see those mini-choppers dropped off at Mars by the space agency's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1) rocket, the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft slated for launch in late 2028. After its cruise phase and initial Mars flyby in 2029, that nuclear carrier craft will make a second Mars approach in the Fall of 2030 to unleash a SkyFall entry capsule outfitted with a fleet of small aerial vehicles that will soar across the Red Planet.

But some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one. "It is clear that SkyFall was approved for programmatic or political reasons," said Scott Hubbard, former director of NASA's Ames Research Center and the first Mars Program Director (aka the "Mars Czar") at NASA Headquarters, told Space.com. "The connection to Space Reactor-1 seems to me to be a bit of a shotgun marriage, a tech-demo piggybacking on another mission as an opening bid for a 'nuclear NASA.'"

Shotgun marriage?

Hubbard is a retired adjunct professor of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University. He is a major voice in shaping Red Planet exploration goals, drawing upon his expertise as NASA's former foremost Mars authority. His understanding is that the basic concept had been developed as a follow on to Ingenuity, an attempt to move beyond a technology demo and into a science platform.

Hubbard said that combining these two observations, the outcome presents "an unusual set of management issues." Since the SkyFall mission concept first appeared, he said, the usual sequence for a science mission is reversed.

"The science community is having to scramble to back into a set of requirements and objectives that match the SkyFall capabilities. Fortunately the community is very creative," said Hubbard, "and the basic Planetary Decadal objectives are very broad."

Decadal surveys reflect a broad consensus within the scientific community and provide detailed insights into the strategic priorities and mission directives set for the next decade across key scientific domains, including planetary exploration.

Lemonade squeeze

However, Hubbard said he has heard griping about the "fait accompli" process, "but the planetary community will make lemonade."

It should be noted however, Hubbard continued, that this process is not how you would design a strategic set of missions as precursors for human exploration.

"SR-1 Freedom is a technology demo that may or may not be ready for the Mars launch window in 2028. It is clear that the Mars Program has a standard launch concept in their back pocket," said Hubbard. "Nuclear Electric Propulsion [NEP] is of little value in traveling to Mars, not shaving any time off the transit. The real value of NEP is for risk reduction, use at the moon, outer planets and even bolder ideas like interstellar travel," Hubbard concluded.

Resolution gap

"This, by far, is the shortest Mars mission ever conceived of," said Matthew Golombek, SkyFall Project Scientist at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, Calif., speaking Nov. 10 during the virtual meeting of the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group (MEPAG).

Kick-started by NASA in March 2026, the SkyFall project has grown from roughly six people to over 200 individuals who are now working on the initiative, said Golombek. "This is an incredibly rapid development and build," he said.

"It's really to demonstrate that exploration is possible with helicopters … filling what I call a 'resolution gap' between orbital information and surface information," Golombek told the MEPAG.

Once deployed by a helicopter deployment system, the threesome will spin up their rotors at about a kilometer above the surface of Mars. Then each helicopter lands on its own, ready to undertake flights every other solar day on the Red Planet. On average, a day (labeled as a sol) on Mars lasts 24 hours 39 minutes 35 seconds, from one noon to the next.

Scientific tasks

SkyFall's prime mission is six months, with a one-year goal," Golombek said, and the intent is to arrive in northern spring on Mars, a time where the vehicles are unlikely to encounter dust storms.

On the to-do list of NASA level one science requisites are for the helicopters to capture high-resolution imagery, perform a set scientific tasks, and help to prepare for future human exploration of Mars, said Golombek.

From their initial landing spots, the whirlybirds could potentially go tens to 100's of kilometers or more in different directions. Identical for all three helicopters, the nominal payload consists of five instruments, plus engineering navigation cameras.

That gear can examine the subsurface structure of Mars, the geomorphology and geology of surface terrains, as well as look at the meteorology of the atmosphere and the planet's radiation environment.

Star of the show

"The real star of the show is ground penetrating radar [GPR] with a flexible antenna," Golombek noted. That ultra-small GPR hardware can look for buried rocks, the layering of the Mars home turf, as well as spot subsurface ice deposits.

"If you have this aerial access and the ability to scout ahead," Golombek said, "you would go a long way towards better defining where to go with a rover and what kind of more detailed surface studies to do with subsequent missions."

All that said, yet to be plotted out are science-focused traverses for the SkyFall helicopters. But there are early ideas.

"The real kicker is that these spacecraft are the smallest landers ever attempted on Mars," said Golombek. "You are looking for a place that virtually has no rocks," he pointed out, a must-have to assure high probability of landing safely. So toss in for good measure low surface slopes, no big craters, a site not overloaded with dust.

Design reference target

One early idea is to revisit the crash locales of discarded SkyFall descent hardware – fuel tanks, cruise stage and associated gear – equipment large and heavy enough to survive entry, smack into the Mars landscape and high-speed and generate craters.

"So if there is ice at centimeters depth, we would create our own icy impact craters," Golombek said. "We could actually visit them in a time-scale before the ice actually sublimates," he said.

Another site getting the eye, albeit deemed a design reference target but considered a "pretty good spot," is within Arcadia Planitia in Mars's northern lowlands. Studies have indicated the presence of substantial volumes of near-surface excess ice there.

"There is a vast amount of information to suggest large quantities of regional ice deposits at that location," said Golombek. "This is at least one location that appears to meet all the engineering constraints and would be a potentially safe landing site…virtually no rocks," he advised.

In the past, Golombek added, JPL took part in SpaceX-sponsored workshops to look for ice deposits as close to the equator of Mars that could be found. Arcadia Planitia was flagged as superior Starship touchdown terrain.

"Most of the landing sites considered for humans have talked about going to places with ice deposits. Ice provides both a consumable as well as fuel to get back off the planet," said Golombek.

On-time delivery

For the near-term, scientific community input next year — via two workshops — are on tap, reviewing the science of SkyFall and also help sort out potential landing sites for final decision-making at NASA Headquarters.

Meanwhile, as SkyFall literally spins up, there is the need for on-time delivery of Space Reactor-1 Freedom.

Golombek said NASA considers the two endeavors as a pair.

"If SR-1 is not ready, SkyFall could be launched on any conventional launch vehicle without any difficulty whatsoever," said Golombek, "something like a Falcon 9 would be more than sufficient, but others are possible as well."

A new supernova has been spotted exploding in the spiral galaxy NGC 1433, about 50 million light-years from Earth.

What is it?

Researchers have discovered a new supernova called SN 2026ahvu. A Type Ia supernova, this event took place in a system with two stars orbiting one another (also known as a binary system), in which typically one star is an exploding white dwarf.

During most type Ia supernovae, the white dwarf pulls material away from the other star until enough accumulates on its surface to create an explosion.

Finding galaxies where stellar explosions are taking place isn't a rarity. However, this supernova is unique in how early it was captured. If the supernova were starting to dim, researchers might infer that the event was ending. However, according to details shared when it was first spotted, as well as later observations, this supernova was discovered while getting brighter.

This indicates that the supernova was likely caught early in the process of exploding, providing researchers with a unique opportunity to observe the event as it is taking place. By exploring observations of the galaxy before, during and (in the future) after the supernova event, researchers can investigate this type Ia supernova and how it affected the system in which it took place.

Why is it incredible?

Scientists made this discovery using ATLAS, or the Asteroid Terrestrial-impact System, which is a robotic astronomical survey made up of telescopes across both hemispheres.

ATLAS is designed to spot incoming near-Earth objects like asteroids before they can reach Earth. It's essentially an asteroid impact early warning system.

But just because that's what the system is designed for doesn't mean that's all it can do. The system can also spot other objects moving through space and, in this instance, it was able to capture observations of this supernova.

Following its initial discovery, other observations of the supernova were made using NOIRLab's Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and Gemini South telescope.

]]> <![CDATA[ India's SatLeo Labs wants to build a 'thermometer for Earth' in space ]]> AHMEDABAD, India — As climate disasters grow more frequent and severe, a young Indian space-tech startup is betting it can help the world act sooner by reading Earth's temperature from orbit in near-real time.

SatLeo Labs, based here in western India, is building what it calls a "thermometer for Earth" in space. It plans to achieve its roadmap to deliver frequent, near-real-time thermal data through Pyro, a planned constellation of 15 microsatellites that will circle the planet in low Earth orbit by early 2030, if all goes to plan. Equipped with thermal sensors and onboard artificial intelligence, the satellites will measure the heat radiating from Earth's surface at a resolution finer than 10 meters (33 feet), which is sharp enough to map heat variations down to street level, the company says.

"It's going to be that precise," SatLeo Labs co-founder Urmil Bakhai told Space.com in a recent interview.

That level of detail, he said, helps distinguish temperatures across a single city and pinpoint urban hot spots, allowing governments and policymakers to plan targeted interventions and more heat-resilient city designs.

The company is also targeting agriculture, and for good reason: Research suggests that thermal data can directly reveal water stress on crops days before leaves wilt, discolor or show other visible damage, unlike visible-light satellite imagery. Other uses the company is eyeing include spotting forest fires early, tracking industrial emissions and, on the defense side, detecting sudden temperature spikes from missile launches.

Down the road, the team also envisions hyper-local uses. Near the top of its list are live heat maps built into navigation apps that could help gig-economy workers in India. These folks, who often ride motorcycles, could use the data to pick cooler routes during heat waves, said Bakhai.

"We are in space, but we're solving problems on Earth," said Shravan Bhati, SatLeo's co-founder and CEO.

First, however, the company has to prove that its homegrown hardware works in space. On Oct. 1, SatLeo launched its first technology demonstrator, TAPAS-1, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket as part of the Transporter-18 rideshare mission. Short for "Thermal Access Platform for Analytics & Solutions," TAPAS-1 is India's first commercial thermal payload in orbit and the first of SatLeo's three planned test payloads meant to validate its technology.

Once complete, the 15-satellite Pyro fleet will scan all of the world's land surface at least twice a day, Bakhai said. Successful deployment of that fleet would make SatLeo one of just a few private thermal-imaging operators across the world, such as SatVu in the U.K. and OroraTech in Germany.

The company has raised roughly $6 million since it was founded in 2023, and it holds letters of intent worth $54 million from prospective customers, Bakhai said.

'Space is the only solution'

SatLeo grew out of a government project that used satellite data for farming insights. Its founders found existing thermal data, such as from the U.S. government's Landsat satellites or Earth-observing craft operated by the San Francisco company Planet Labs, too coarse for India's fragmented farmlands, Bakhai said. When field teams and drones couldn't fill the gap at scale, "we realized space is the only solution," he said.

SatLeo's orbital ambitions take shape on the ground, inside a light-blocked cleanroom at the company's headquarters here in Ahmedabad. When Space.com visited in late October, about three weeks after TAPAS-1 launched, a handful of engineers in cleanroom coats were already fine-tuning its successor, TAPAS-2.

The payload itself sat perched on a solitary, nondescript table with a thick, hole-filled steel top meant to dampen vibrations from footsteps, traffic and the like. The room's only window was covered by a thick black blind to seal out stray light, a necessity for calibrating sensors meant to track the planet's thermal pulse from a few hundred kilometers up.

Despite its small size, the payload is built to collect enormous amounts of data. How much detail a payload can capture "all depends upon the architecture of the detector," said SatLeo co-founder Ranendu Ghosh, a former scientist at the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).

The design captures two infrared bands, mid-wave and long-wave, on the same payload. The company says this lets a single design serve both civilian and defense uses: long-wave suits applications like agriculture, while the hotter signatures of fires or missile launches show up better in mid-wave.

'Zeal to deliver in time'

TAPAS-1 took just six months to build, and TAPAS-2 is on a similar timeline: It's expected to be ready by February 2027, according to the team.

Access to government test facilities explains much of that speed, Bhati said. Rather than buy capital-intensive equipment, such as a thermal vacuum chamber that mimics conditions in space, the company calibrates its payloads at facilities run by IN-SPACe, the government agency that supports private space firms, and ISRO's Space Applications Centre, both in Ahmedabad.

A small group of former ISRO scientists, about eight among a staff of around 40, also mentored the younger workforce and "really made this journey a little faster for us," Bakhai said.

Ghosh, who spent more than two decades at ISRO, said the nature of a private company helps, too. "When I was in ISRO, I saw people delivering this kind of a payload," he said. "I never saw it delivered in less than a year."

He credited the SatLeo team's "zeal to deliver in time," along with fewer administrative challenges than at ISRO, which he described as an organization where "you cannot bypass the hierarchy."

The harder constraint, the founders said, is not building satellites but finding rockets to carry them to space. TAPAS-1's launch slipped from a planned February liftoff to October for lack of a ride, Bakhai said.

SpaceX is reportedly not accepting new bookings until at least 2029. In addition, Skyroot Aerospace, which in July became the first Indian company to reach orbit, is still flying development missions meant to validate its Vikram-1 rocket before it begins full-scale commercial operations.

"There is a challenge right now in terms of availability of launch vehicles," Bakhai said. Once additional Indian rockets, such as those built by Skyroot and Agnikul, are flying regularly, "things will be much easier."

SatLeo is among more than 400 space startups that have emerged in India since the government opened the sector to private participation in 2020. Driven by this new wave of private enterprise, the country's space economy — currently valued at about $9 billion — is estimated to reach $40 billion over the next decade.

Asked what advice they would give newcomers entering the growing industry, SatLeo's three co-founders offered a unified message for success: start with the problem, then decide what to build.

"If you're solving a problem," Bhati said, "then people will bet on you."

A small group of former ISRO scientists, about eight among a staff of around 40, also mentored the younger workforce and "really made this journey a little faster for us," Bakhai said.

Ghosh, who spent more than two decades at ISRO, said the nature of a private company helps, too. "When I was in ISRO, I saw people delivering this kind of a payload," he said. "I never saw it delivered in less than a year."

He credited the SatLeo team's "zeal to deliver in time," along with fewer administrative challenges than at ISRO, which he described as an organization where "you cannot bypass the hierarchy."

The harder constraint, the founders said, is not building satellites but finding rockets to carry them to space. TAPAS-1's launch slipped from a planned February liftoff to October for lack of a ride, Bakhai said.

SpaceX is reportedly not accepting new bookings until at least 2029. In addition, Skyroot Aerospace, which in July became the first Indian company to reach orbit, is still flying development missions meant to validate its Vikram-1 rocket before it begins full-scale commercial operations.

"There is a challenge right now in terms of availability of launch vehicles," Bakhai said. Once additional Indian rockets, such as those built by Skyroot and Agnikul, are flying regularly, "things will be much easier."

SatLeo is among more than 400 space startups that have emerged in India since the government opened the sector to private participation in 2020. Driven by this new wave of private enterprise, the country's space economy — currently valued at about $9 billion — is estimated to reach $40 billion over the next decade.

Asked what advice they would give newcomers entering the growing industry, SatLeo's three co-founders offered a unified message for success: start with the problem, then decide what to build.

"If you're solving a problem," Bhati said, "then people will bet on you."

<title>GTA 6 přepsalo rekord českého internetu, proteklo jím nejvíce dat v historii</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/gta-6-prepsalo-rekord-ceskeho-internetu-proteklo-jim-nejvice-dat-v-historii/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Českým internetem dnes protekl rekordní počet dat. Tuzemský nezávislý internetový uzel NIX.CZ, v rámci něhož si operátoři, poskytovatelé internetu, webových služeb a podobně vyměňují data, pokořil hranici čtyř terabitů za sekundu (4 Tb/s). NIX už se k tomu párkrát přiblížil, dnes po osmé hodině večerní se to konečně podařilo.</description>

<description>Růst jedné z nejnadějněj&#353;ích českých technologických společností neustále zrychluje. <description>Digitální stanice Českého rozhlasu Radiožurnál Sport poprvé dosáhla hranice 100 tisíc posluchačů v průměrném dni. Dosavadní maximum překonal také Český rozhlas Plus. <description>Online projekt Knihobot, který vykupuje a nabízí přečtené knihy, vstupuje pod značkou Bookbot.pl oficiálně na polský trh. K výročí města</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905921-do-jabloneckych-zahrad-zamirilo-160-jabloni-starych-odrud-k-vyroci-mesta.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905921-do-jabloneckych-zahrad-zamirilo-160-jabloni-starych-odrud-k-vyroci-mesta.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 19:55:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Jablonec nad Nisou rozdal v uplynulých dnech obyvatelům 160 sazenic tradičních odrůd jabloní, každou za symbolickou cenu 160 korun. Projekt připomínající 160 let od povýšení Jablonce na město má vrátit odolné stromy zpět do místních zahrad.</description></item><item><title>Auto se u Spálova zřítilo ze srázu, těžce zraněnou řidičku vyprostili hasiči</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906118-auto-se-u-spalova-zritilo-ze-srazu-tezce-zranenou-ridicku-vyprostili-hasici.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906118-auto-se-u-spalova-zritilo-ze-srazu-tezce-zranenou-ridicku-vyprostili-hasici.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 19:01:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>K vážné nehodě došlo ve středu odpoledne na Semilsku. Auto se na silnici 288 u Spálova zřítilo ze srázu ke korytu řeky Kamenice. Řidička zůstala ve voze zaklíněná, zranil se i spolujezdec.</description></item><item><title>Předvánoční nákupy lákají i kyberzločince. Podvodům čelila většina Čechů, varují experti</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906061-predvanocni-nakupy-lakaji-i-kyberzlocince-podvodum-celila-vetsina-cechu-varuji-experti.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906061-predvanocni-nakupy-lakaji-i-kyberzlocince-podvodum-celila-vetsina-cechu-varuji-experti.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 18:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Michael Daněk</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>S blížícími se Vánocemi a slevovými akcemi Black Friday roste také riziko internetových podvodů. S některou formou kybernetického útoku se v posledních 12 měsících setkalo 62 procent dospělých Čechů. Nejčastěji šlo o spamové nabídky, následovaly podvodné e-maily. Vyplývá to z aktuálního výzkumu.</description></item><item><title>Tomáš Arsov zavítá s Rossmann Tour do Liberce</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905700-tomas-arsov-zavita-s-rossmann-tour-do-liberce.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905700-tomas-arsov-zavita-s-rossmann-tour-do-liberce.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:55:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Tomáš Arsov zamíří ve středu 25. listopadu 2026 do Liberce. Od 16.30 do 19.00 se setká s návštěvníky v obchodním centru Nisa, představí vlasové tonery a péči COLOR CARE. Vstup je zdarma a bez registrace.</description></item><item><title>Liberecký Strom přání slaví dvacet let. Lidé ho najdou v Paláci Liebieg</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906066-liberecky-strom-prani-slavi-dvacet-let-lide-ho-najdou-v-palaci-liebieg.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906066-liberecky-strom-prani-slavi-dvacet-let-lide-ho-najdou-v-palaci-liebieg.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Tradiční předvánoční akce v Liberci vstupuje do svého dvacátého ročníku. Od 18. listopadu do 20. prosince mohou děti i dospělí zavěsit své tajné tužby na Strom přání na nádvoří Paláce Liebieg. Několik vylosovaných šťastlivců se dočká splnění svého snu v lednu na radnici.</description></item><item><title>Nečekejte na první sníh. Do hor vyrazte na zimních pneumatikách</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905933-necekejte-na-prvni-snih-do-hor-vyrazte-na-zimnich-pneumatikach.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905933-necekejte-na-prvni-snih-do-hor-vyrazte-na-zimnich-pneumatikach.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:02:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Doprava</category><description>Zimní výbava není jen otázkou pneumatik. Při cestách do horských oblastí se vyplatí myslet také na sněhové řetězy, základní nouzovou výbavu a možná omezení na silnicích. Některé úseky v Libereckém kraji navíc vyžadují zimní pneumatiky bez ohledu na aktuální počasí.</description></item><item><title>Hrajeme v Liberci. Kampaň propojuje fotbalový Slovan a divadlo F.X. Šaldy</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906074-hrajeme-v-liberci-kampan-propojuje-fotbalovy-slovan-a-divadlo-f-x-saldy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906074-hrajeme-v-liberci-kampan-propojuje-fotbalovy-slovan-a-divadlo-f-x-saldy.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:29:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Liberecký Slovan společně s Divadlem F. X. Šaldy představili novou originální kampaň, která oba světy propojuje. A představili ji částečně v klubovém autobuse a částečně ve foyer divadla. Lidé na kampaň narazí ve městě, na sociálních sítích, ale i přímo na stadionu a v divadle.</description></item><item><title>Liberecké vánoční trhy ozdobí skleněný sněhulák. Lidé mu mohou vybrat jméno</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906028-liberecke-vanocni-trhy-ozdobi-skleneny-snehulak-lide-mu-mohou-vybrat-jmeno.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906028-liberecke-vanocni-trhy-ozdobi-skleneny-snehulak-lide-mu-mohou-vybrat-jmeno.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Novým maskotem libereckých vánočních trhů se letos stane originální skleněný sněhulák z dílny uměleckého skláře Jiřího Pačinka. Pořadatelé nyní vyzývají veřejnost, aby mu pomohla vybrat jméno v online anketě. Hlasovat můžete až do 24. listopadu.</description></item><item><title>Nové semafory v centru Liberce. Rostou u knihovny</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906018-nove-semafory-v-centru-liberce-rostou-u-knihovny.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906018-nove-semafory-v-centru-liberce-rostou-u-knihovny.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 06:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>V centru města přibude nová světelná křižovatka. Na křižovatce ulic Sokolská a Nová Pastýřská pod knihovnou už rostou semafory. Hotovo má být v polovině prosince.</description></item><item><title>Problém bazénu v Jablonci. Šatnářky nevpustily ženu se synem, muž si měl fotit děti</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906013-problem-bazenu-v-jablonci-satnarky-nevpustily-zenu-se-synem-muz-si-mel-fotit-deti.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906013-problem-bazenu-v-jablonci-satnarky-nevpustily-zenu-se-synem-muz-si-mel-fotit-deti.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 19:42:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Jablonecký bazén musí řešit nepříjemnou kauzu. Markéta Krbková na sociálních sítích upozornila na to, že nebyla vpuštěna do dámské šatny se sedmiletým synem. Podle ní pak měl do bazénu chodit muž, který si ve sprchách fotil děti.</description></item></channel></rss>

NOVÉ ZASTUPITELSTVO JIŘÍKOVA ZAHÁJILO SVÉ VOLEBNÍ OBDOBÍ
(Jiříkovské noviny listopad 2026)
V pondělí 9. 11. 2026 se uskutečnilo ustavující zasedání Zastupitelstva města Jiříkov, které zahájilo nové čtyřleté volební období 2026–2030. Na programu bylo především složení slibu nově zvolených zastupitelů, volba vedení města a dalších orgánů samosprávy.
Po složení zákonem předepsaného slibu přistoupili zastupitelé k volbě starosty a místostarosty města. Starostou Jiříkova byl zvolen a svou funkci tak obhájil Ing. Bc. Jindřich Jurajda, DiS. Zastupitelstvo dále zvolilo členy Rady města Jiříkov. Jejími členy se stali Mgr. Michal Mrázek a Jaroslav Vöröš (NEZÁVISLÍ KANDIDÁTI MĚSTA JIŘÍKOVA) a Ing. Nikol Kopecká (Spolek přátel Jiříkova a Filipova). Součástí jednání byla také volba předsedů a členů finančního a kontrolního výboru. V čele finančního výboru usedla stejně jako v minulém volebním období Naděžda Stožická (NEZÁVISLÍ KANDIDÁTI MĚSTA JIŘÍKOVA) a předsedou kontrolního výboru se stal Mgr. Petr Kulhánek MBA (ANO 2011).
Nově zvolené vedení města tak přebírá odpovědnost za další rozvoj Jiříkova, hospodaření s městským majetkem, přípravu a realizaci investičních projektů i každodenní chod městské samosprávy.
Nové zastupitelstvo tvoří celkem 15 členů zvolených za čtyři kandidující uskupení. Jejich společným úkolem bude rozhodovat o důležitých otázkách života města a zastupovat zájmy jeho obyvatel.
Všem nově zvoleným zastupitelům přejeme hodně sil, trpělivosti a úspěchů při práci pro Jiříkov a jeho občany.

SPOLEČNĚ PRO VELKÝ ŠENOV
Komunální volby jsou důležitou součástí života našeho města. Děkujeme všem občanům, kteří přišli k volebním urnám a využili svého práva rozhodnout o budoucím směřování Velkého Šenova.

Před námi jsou další čtyři roky práce, důležitých rozhodnutí, nových projektů i pokračování těch rozpracovaných. Věříme, že společným úsilím, konstruktivní spoluprací a otevřenou komunikací dokážeme Velký Šenov nadále rozvíjet jako příjemné místo pro život všech generací.
